a100.name: A100 80GB (DGX A100 nodes)
a100.source: Narayanan et al. 2021 §5 (312 TFLOP/s; eight 200 Gb/s HDR InfiniBand cards per 8-GPU node, so 25 GB/s per GPU); NVLink 600 GB/s total per GPU (A100 datasheet), 300 GB/s each way

h100.name: H100 80GB (8-GPU servers)
h100.source: 989 TFLOP/s dense BF16 and NVLink 900 GB/s total (H100 SXM datasheet); 400 Gb/s per GPU (Grattafiori et al. 2024 §3.3.1), so 50 GB/s

reliability.deltaNote: 16,384 GPUs x 4 GB at the storage fabric's 2 TB/s sustained (Llama 3 §3.3.1)
reliability.restartNote: illustrative: 10 minutes to restart and reload

assumptions.bytes: BF16 (2 bytes) for activations, parameters and gradients on the wire
assumptions.flops: Megatron rows: equation (3) of Narayanan et al. (with full recomputation); Llama rows: the PaLM MFU count 6N + 12 L H Q T per token (no recomputation)
assumptions.interleave: v = layers per pipeline rank (one layer per model chunk), the most interleaving the layer count allows; Llama 3 counts 128 layer slots (126 layers + the embedding and output stages, its §3.3.2)
assumptions.latency: 5 us per NVLink hop, 10 us per network hop (Llama 3 §3.3.3: 'latency up to tens of microseconds' across a large cluster)
assumptions.microBatch: 1 sequence per micro-batch (neither paper gives it for these runs)
assumptions.overlap: nothing overlaps: every collective, send and the gradient sync is exposed
